documents.abstract: The article is devoted to the study of the process of land plot allocation using modern geodetic equipment. The relevance of the topic is due to the fact that errors made during allocation lead to inaccuracies in the actual boundaries, area and status of the plot, cause overlapping of plots, litigation and problems with land development and construction. The study examines the regulatory framework governing the allocation procedure in the Russian Federation, considers traditional and modern technologies, and describes the methodology of geodetic works using GNSS equipment. Using the example of a land plot with cadastral number 14:35:211001:3291, located on the Vilyuysky tract in the urban district "City of Yakutsk", the boundaries were set out using two GNSS receivers EFT M4 in RTK mode with reference to the point "Pakhay2" in the MSK-14 coordinate system. Typical errors are identified: violation of gas pipeline protection zones, registry errors, errors related to the human factor, multipath and GPS spoofing. It is established that traditional methods using an optical total station require line of sight, the work of a two-person crew and are subject to instrumental and human errors, whereas GNSS receivers and robotic total stations provide centimeter accuracy and high productivity. For areas with a low density of geodetic networks, the PPK method with post-processing of data is effective. It is concluded that it is necessary to integrate modern geodetic technologies, carefully verify source data and strictly comply with regulatory requirements in order to minimize allocation errors.

Purpose Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in clinical data workflows, but most clinicians lack the time, training, or support to build predictive models. We evaluated whether a ChatGPT-assisted workflow could enable clinicians to independently construct and execute a basic predictive model using routine perioperative data, using postoperative length of stay (LOS) in pediatric appendicitis as a feasibility use case. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of 228 children undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy. Ten routinely available preoperative variables were used. ChatGPT guided preprocessing and generated code for linear regression and random forest models using naïve and structured prompting. Models were trained using an 80/20 split and evaluated using MAE, RMSE, r, and R 2 . Results Naïve prompting performed poorly, while structured prompting improved model performance (MAE 0.34, RMSE 0.85, r 0.85). On the test set, linear regression achieved MAE 1.00 and random forest 0.77. Identified variables reflected expected clinical patterns. These findings demonstrate internal consistency of the workflow rather than new predictive insight. Conclusions A structured ChatGPT workflow enabled clinicians to construct standard predictive models using routine data. These findings support feasibility of clinician-directed model development, but not clinical utility, of LLM-enabled workflows.

documents.abstract: Background Patients increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to seek medical information, but their performance in answering diabetic retinopathy (DR) questions remains insufficiently characterized. Objective To evaluate the safety, accuracy, patient-centered communication, information quality, transparency, and readability of diabetic retinopathy information generated by widely accessible large language models. Methods Fifty standardized DR patient questions were submitted to ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Doubao, Copilot, and Perplexity. Responses were independently evaluated by five raters using guideline-based reference answer elements. Rater-based outcomes included Safety, Accuracy, Empathy, DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark criteria, and Global Quality Score (GQS). Readability was assessed using the Automated Readability Index, Coleman–Liau Index, Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level, Gunning Fog Index, SMOG, and Flesch Reading Ease Score. Inter-rater agreement and between-model differences were analyzed using appropriate agreement statistics and paired nonparametric tests. Results Inter-rater agreement was moderate for Safety (Fleiss’ κ = 0.581) and good for non-binary outcomes, with ICC (2,1) values ranging from 0.806 to 0.870. Most responses were classified as safe, with safe response rates ranging from 86.0 to 94.0%, and no significant between-model difference was observed. Accuracy scores were generally high across models, although between-model differences were statistically significant with a small effect size. Empathy varied more noticeably, with Copilot scoring highest and Doubao and Perplexity scoring lower. Perplexity achieved the highest DISCERN and JAMA scores, while Copilot performed best on EQIP. GQS differences were small. Readability differed significantly across models, with Gemini generally producing the most readable responses; however, all models exceeded the recommended sixth-grade reading level, and all Flesch Reading Ease Scores were below the recommended threshold. Conclusion No single LLM performed best across all domains. Although the evaluated models generally provided safe and accurate responses to DR patient questions, limitations remained in safety escalation, empathy, transparency, and readability. LLM-generated DR information may support general patient education but should not replace professional ophthalmic consultation.

documents.abstract: This article argues that the persistent burden of burnout reflects a fundamental conceptual problem—burnout continues to be framed primarily as an individual condition rather than as an occupational phenomenon shaped by interacting structural, organizational, and leadership conditions. Burnout has emerged as a major occupational health challenge. In a 2024 survey across eight predominantly high and upper-middle-income countries, 48% of respondents reported currently grappling with burnout. Separately, depression and anxiety cost the global economy approximately one trillion dollars annually in lost productivity. Drawing on evidence from neuroimaging, stress biology, cognitive neuroscience, and organizational research, this article examines plausible pathways through which leadership behavior may influence conditions that contribute to or protect against burnout, including social threat–reward processing, cognitive flexibility, emotional intelligence, psychological safety, emotional contagion, and stress-related neurobiological responses. Among physicians, burnout has been associated with depression and anxiety, while evidence regarding substance abuse is less consistent. These proposed mechanisms are proximal and potentially modifiable, but operate within broader structural conditions that constrain or enable their effects. Human-centered work design and neuroleadership-informed leadership practices are proposed as complements to broader structural interventions, with implications for health systems, workforce sustainability, and policy design.

Knowledge graph embedding aims to predict missing links by learning representations of entities and relations. However, existing methods often struggle to effectively capture interaction features at multiple scales and to suppress redundant information among these multi-scale features, which hinders the model’s ability to focus on essential semantics. They also neglect the sensitivity of entities under specific relations, resulting in the lack of discriminability of entity representations. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel A ttention-enhanced R elation-sensitive V ariable receptive field-aware knowledge graph E mbedding method ( ARVE ). In this study, ARVE adopts a hybrid multi-scale grouped convolution module that extends the receptive fields of kernels in different forms to capture interaction features at multiple scales. Subsequently, ARVE introduces a feature points–convolutional kernels joint selection mechanism, which adaptively assigns weights to both convolutional kernels and specific feature locations, optimizing the adaptive fusion process of the aforementioned multi-scale features. Furthermore, a global attention block is employed to produce relation-sensitive entity representations by computing relevance scores between them, while modeling global dependencies. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that ARVE possesses a remarkable capability to capture information from local to global. It achieves notable performance across several benchmarks. In particular, on FB15k-237, ARVE improves MRR by 15.5% compared with the strongest graph neural network-based baseline DGATCL and by 6.6% compared with the overall strongest LLM-based baseline GLTW. Our code is available at https://github.com/JasmineMina07/ARVE .

Blended learning, which integrates face-to-face instruction with technology-mediated online components, has gained prominence as schools seek flexible and learner-centred pedagogies. This study examined the effect of a blended learning approach on the academic achievement and classroom engagement of secondary school students in Kerala, India. A quasi-experimental, non-equivalent control group design was employed with 120 ninth-grade students drawn from two comparable government-aided schools. The experimental group (n = 60) received eight weeks of blended instruction combining classroom teaching with a learning management system, interactive video lessons, and online formative quizzes, while the control group (n = 60) received conventional lecture-based instruction. Academic achievement was measured using a validated 40-item subject achievement test administered as pre-test and post-test, and engagement was assessed with a 20-item student engagement scale measuring behavioural, emotional, and cognitive dimensions. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), controlling for pre-test scores, revealed a statistically significant difference in post-test achievement favouring the experimental group (F = 28.64, p < .001), with a large effect size (partial eta squared = .20). The blended learning group also reported significantly higher engagement across all three dimensions, with the largest gain in cognitive engagement. Findings suggest that a well-structured blended approach can enhance both learning outcomes and engagement at the secondary level. The study recommends sustained teacher training in blended pedagogy and improved digital infrastructure, and discusses implications for classroom practice, curriculum design, and education policy.

Natural-image-pretrained foundation models are increasingly adapted to medical imaging, yet transfer remains unreliable under domain shift, modality heterogeneity, and label scarcity. We trace part of this fragility to an overlooked design choice. Standard vision transformers place all global modeling on self-attention over spatial tokens, an object-layout prior well suited to natural scenes but not to medical images, where the discriminative signal lies in feature correlations and texture that recur across scanners while layout does not. We ask whether the axis of global attention, spatial versus feature, is itself a lever for transferable medical representations. Existing channel-aware hybrids confound this question, adding channel attention to a spatially-mixed backbone and leaving the axes coupled and the feature axis unmeasurable in isolation. We design FAD-ViT, a backbone that strictly decouples the two axes, making feature-axis attention the primary global operator and the attention axis a controlled variable. Evaluating comprehensively across 23 classification, segmentation, and low-data tasks under matched tokenization, capacity, and protocol, we find that shifting global attention from the spatial to the feature axis leaves from-scratch performance essentially unchanged, yet markedly strengthens transfer. Identical ImageNet pretraining yields up to roughly three times the transfer gain, with consistent improvements on every held-out segmentation task at up to a quarter the parameter count and far lower compute than standard and channel-attention baselines. The advantage is largest where texture rather than geometry is discriminative, tracking greater reuse of pretrained features. The axis of global attention is thus a design lever for medical transfer, and making it channel-primary is a simple, cheap, and principled choice.

Large language models have achieved remarkable advances in complex reasoning. However, scaling reasoning post-training with ever-larger corpora can substantially increase training cost without proportional performance gains. In this study, we therefore ask: how far can reasoning supervision be compressed without sacrificing capability? To this end, we propose an uncertainty-guided progressive contraction framework that concentrates supervision and optimization on the reasoning trajectories most valuable for learning. Specifically, rather than treating a teacher-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) as a single realized path, we construct uncertainty-profiled reasoning supervision by building Monte Carlo reasoning trees around intermediate reasoning states to expose process-level uncertainty. This uncertainty first contracts the original corpus into a compact teacher-informed pool. A second, learner-aware contraction then performs online routing during SFT, concentrating optimization according to the student's evolving learning state. Together, the two stages progressively contract both supervision and optimization, substantially reducing the student training budget. Experiments across diverse reasoning benchmarks and LLM families show that our method uses as little as 0.22% of the optimization budget of full-data SFT, over 450x less training exposure, while maintaining or improving reasoning performance. Notably, our framework generalizes well across heterogeneous student families, black-box teachers, and weak-to-strong transfer. This indicates that it is not only a way to accelerate training but can also enhance reasoning capability.

Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly becoming part of engineering students’ learning environments, particularly in quantitative problem solving, explanation generation, and formative feedback. The educational value of these systems, however, depends not only on output accuracy but also on whether learners can evaluate claims that appear authoritative. This paper proposes Deliberate Ambiguity Verification (DAV), an instructional framework in which electrical engineering students compare two AI-generated solutions that are mathematically plausible and professionally presented but differ in a consequential assumption, boundary condition, or physical interpretation. Students must identify the point of divergence, verify each response against an independent engineering principle, justify a decision, and report confidence before and after verification. The framework integrates epistemic vigilance, trust calibration, metacognitive monitoring, cognitive engagement, productive failure, and discipline-specific AI literacy. A randomized four-condition design is proposed for students in circuit analysis, contrasting no-AI problem solving, a single AI answer, a plausible-but-incorrect AI answer, and deliberate ambiguity. Primary outcomes are conceptual reasoning, verification behavior, confidence calibration, and AI-free transfer. The paper argues that the goal should not be generalized distrust of AI, but calibrated skepticism: the capacity to determine when an AI response should be accepted provisionally, when it requires independent verification, and when disciplinary reasoning should override the apparent authority of the system. The framework is intended to provide a testable pathway for studying epistemically responsible human-AI collaboration in engineering education.

This study examines how foreign firms strategically manage the salience of foreignness when facing unfavorable domestic evaluators. Foreign firms do so by altering the ethnic composition of the agents representing them before the evaluators. We examine this question in the context of Asian firms’ selection of legal counsel in U.S. federal courts. Prior research suggests that foreign firms may anticipate less favorable evaluations in courts that have historically favored domestic over foreign firms and in those with conservative judges. We argue that, in such evaluative settings, Asian firms adjust the ethnic composition of their external legal teams to manage the salience of foreignness, and that such adjustments are especially likely in courts that combine judge conservatism with pro-domestic ruling histories. We test these arguments using data on U.S. patent litigation from 2000 to 2016 and validated measures of courts’ political ideology and pro-domestic ruling histories. We find that Asian firms reduce the proportion of Asian-origin lawyers and increase the proportion of White lawyers when litigating in conservative courts, particularly when these courts also have pro-domestic ruling histories. By contrast, the ethnic composition of lawyers representing domestic firms remains stable across courts. Evidence of implicit bias against Asians among legal professionals provides additional support consistent with the theorized mechanism. Post-hoc analyses reveal that adjusting the ethnic composition of external legal teams attenuates the likelihood of unfavorable outcomes in conservative courts. These findings contribute to research on liability of foreignness by identifying agent selection as a specific mitigation mechanism in evaluative arenas.

The rapid evolution of high-throughput sequencing technologies has effectively transformed DNA sequencers into advanced genomic biosensors. However, the accurate functional annotation and classification of raw DNA sequences directly from these biosensor outputs, without manual feature extraction, remain central challenges in computational genomics. While deep learning methods have shown remarkable success in specialized tasks, such as viral genome detection in complex sensor-derived biological samples, a comprehensive evaluation of how diverse architectural paradigms generalize across varied genomic sensing contexts warrants further investigation. In this study, we extend beyond domain-specific models by benchmarking a broad spectrum of deep learning architectures, ranging from pure Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and self-attention mechanisms to hybrid CNN-Transformer frameworks and pre-trained genomic foundation models (DNABERT-2) augmented with motif-refinement modules; moreover, we propose a novel hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture. Furthermore, we develop a comprehensive ensemble strategy that integrates these diverse architectures while systematically varying key training hyperparameters, including data augmentation techniques and loss functions, to optimize predictive performance. We evaluate models across a diverse suite of genomic datasets, encompassing viral host classification, Escherichia coli promoter recognition, and human enhancer classification. Our comparative analysis highlights the relative trade-offs between convolutional local feature extraction and attention-based global context modeling when processing high-dimensional sequence data acquired by genomic sensors. The results demonstrate that ensemble and attention-guided models consistently achieve superior generalization and robustness across distinct genomic classification tasks, providing a systematic framework for robust computational analysis of sequencing derived DNA sequences.

Recent progress in real-time communication frameworks has significantly advanced the development of multimodal intelligent assistants that can interact with users in a natural, human-like manner.This paper introduces a LiveKit-based AI Assistant designed to enable seamless, low-latency human-computer interaction by integrating real-time audio streaming, large language model (LLM) reasoning, and automated system control within a unified architecture.The proposed framework utilizes LiveKit Agents for real-time connectivity, employs noise suppression plugins for robust speech processing, and leverages LangChain-based orchestration to ensure contextual understanding and reasoning [1], [2].In addition, the assistant incorporates a versatile toolkit for web-based search, voice-command interpretation, and operating system-level automation, enabling it to function effectively across diverse platforms and environments.Experimental evaluations indicate that the system achieves high responsiveness and scalability while maintaining lightweight deployment characteristics.Compared to existing conversational agents such as traditional virtual assistants, the proposed model offers superior customizability, cross-platform adaptability, and real-time feedback performance.This research underscores the potential of LiveKit-powered multimodal agents in shaping the future of real-time interactive AI systems suitable for both academic exploration and real-world deployment [3], [4].

Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.

This article examines the linguacultural aspect in languages of different systems. Although the study of euphemisms began in the history of ancient Greek and Roman linguistics, a new era of their study began in the 20th century with the application of the anthropocentric method of research. The advent of cognitive linguistics also ushered in a new era of euphemism research. It was established that the pragmatic and linguacultural approach to euphemisms differed significantly from pre- 20th-century research in both content and the characteristics of communicative activity, as well as in its linguacultural nature. The essence was that, in addition to the general characteristics of euphemisms, their role in communicative activity began to be studied; the essence of semantic substitutions from the perspective of the speech act was revealed. It is noted that problems noted in English and Azerbaijani linguistics in the modern period have begun to be theoretically studied. It has been proven that, in particular, a linguacultural approach to euphemisms and the study of the fundamental concepts of cognitive linguistics in this context have given new impetus to the development of lexicology. This article has somewhat modernized the approach to the problem, provided a historical overview of euphemism research, and analyzed semantic associations and their cultural roots based on facts from the English and Azerbaijani languages. The complete formation of anthropocentric linguistics in linguistics at the end of the 20th century and the beginning of the 21st century created a turning point in the scientific study of euphemisms; the prominent feeling of the human factor in the study of the problem confirmed the necessity of pragmatic and linguocultural approaches to the problem. With the emergence of cognitive linguistics, no matter how many studies in these directions have increased and deep studies have been conducted, it is still impossible to consider the problem fully studied, as each research method emerges, it opens up new aspects of language problems, and as they are studied, cognitive linguistics is enriched with new theoretical facts.

ABSTRACT This paper presents a comprehensive review of live‐line work on high‐voltage transmission overhead lines, with a focus on insulation performance, air‐gap breakdown and discharge physics under realistic operating conditions. This review primarily covers journal publications from approximately 2014 to 2026, with emphasis on recent developments in the field. Despite the critical importance of live‐line maintenance for power system reliability, the number of peer‐reviewed journal studies remains relatively limited, and this work aims to consolidate the majority of available contributions within this period. Key topics include flashover mechanisms of fibreglass‐reinforced polymer hot sticks under cold and freezing conditions, physics‐based modelling of long air‐gap breakdown under switching‐impulse voltages and the influence of tower geometry, worker configuration and hybrid AC/DC systems on insulation performance. In addition, multi‐worker interaction, floating‐conductor effects, potential transfer mechanisms and high‐altitude conditions are examined. Fundamental discharge processes, including streamer inception, streamer‐to‐leader transition and leader propagation, are reviewed to establish a unified physical framework. Collectively, the reviewed studies demonstrate that live‐line insulation performance is governed by coupled electrostatic, thermal, environmental and geometric effects. This review provides a consolidated reference for the field, identifies the need for integrated multiphysics modelling approaches to improve safety criteria, standards development and minimum approach distance determination, and discusses emerging developments in helicopter‐assisted maintenance, advanced access techniques, monitoring and diagnostic technologies, artificial intelligence‐assisted tools and digital approaches that may contribute to safer and more efficient live‐line maintenance in future power systems.

documents.abstract: The rapid globalization of news media has heightened the demand for high-quality, culturally adapted international news content. However, generating news articles that faithfully conform to the stylistic conventions of diverse national media outlets while maintaining cross-cultural semantic fidelity remains a formidable challenge. This paper presents a novel framework that leverages fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) for international news style generation and introduces a comprehensive cross-cultural dissemination quality assessment (CDQA) methodology. Specifically, we construct a multilingual international news corpus spanning seven major languages and ten distinct journalistic style profiles, drawn from leading international media organizations. We then apply parameter-efficient fine-tuning via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on a LLaMA-2-based backbone, augmented with a style-aware prefix adapter that conditions generation on target-style embeddings. For quality assessment, we propose a multi-dimensional evaluation framework integrating automatic metrics—including BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, and BERTScore—with a novel Cross-Cultural Appropriateness Score (CCAS) grounded in culturological theory. Experimental results demonstrate that our fine-tuned model achieves a BLEU-4 score of 42.7 and a BERTScore F1 of 0.876 on held-out test sets, outperforming strong baselines by 5.3 and 3.1 percentage points, respectively. Human evaluation conducted by bilingual journalists across five language pairs yields mean fluency and cultural appropriateness ratings of 4.21/5.00 and 4.08/5.00, respectively. Cross-cultural quality classification accuracy reaches 87.3%, validating the effectiveness of the CCAS framework. This work offers a scalable, reproducible pipeline for high-fidelity international news generation, with direct implications for global media localization.

documents.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) can make robot programming more intuitive by letting users set motion parameters directly in the workspace. This paper extends AURaPath, an AR system for interactive 6-DoF waypoint determination on a UR10 collaborative robot using HoloLens2, with a voice modality for hands-free authoring. The voice layer follows a two-tier design: an on-device keyword recognizer handles the safety-critical verbs behind a two-step confirmation gate, and a large language model (LLM) maps the resulting transcript to the system’s structured command set so that operators need not memorize fixed phrases; the deployed pipeline takes spoken microphone input, while the benchmark below evaluates the transcript-to-command mapping stage in isolation. We evaluate the mapping layer on an objective benchmark of 169 labeled utterances that isolates language-to-command mapping from speech recognition and robot execution, and we compare a deterministic keyword baseline, four local models on a single consumer GPU, and free-tier cloud backends. The keyword baseline cannot express parameterized authoring commands and scores zero on every authoring field, while a free-tier cloud model reaches 95.3% exact-match results, averaged over 10 runs. The reject analysis shows that the ability to decline out-of-scope input, rather than raw accuracy, determines whether a model is suitable for the language-mapping tier of our safety-gated architecture, in which a deterministic layer and a preview-before-execute gate remain responsible for execution, which supports keeping the safety-critical verbs on the deterministic layer. The benchmark selects the backend that the deployed system uses, on the same physical UR10 demonstrated in the base system. The project code, the evaluation harness and dataset, and the base-system demonstration are available on GitHub (Please see Data Availability Statement section).

Abstract Privacy auditing has emerged as a critical component for safeguarding data privacy in machine learning models. Existing empirical auditing methods heavily rely on model runtime states or post-deployment interfaces, resulting in substantial time costs and limited source-level localization of leakage causes. In contrast, the theoretical guarantees of provable privacy mechanisms provide a basis for efficient privacy auditing with source-level traceability before model training. However, the validity of such auditing depends on the semantic consistency of the underlying implementation, which remains difficult for current automated methods to verify due to limited privacy-specific reasoning and explicit evidence modeling. To address this gap, we formalize the Pre-execution Privacy Auditing paradigm and instantiate it for DP-SGD through LLMDPA, an automated framework based on evidence-constrained semantic analysis. LLMDPA constructs a structured Evidence Chain to constrain LLM-based adjudication and identify hidden semantic failures in DP-SGD implementations. Evaluations on real-world and controlled benchmarks show that LLMDPA achieves global precision ranging from 98.82 to 100% and global F1-scores ranging from 0.9091 to 0.9677 across four LLM configurations, outperforming conventional static and vanilla LLM baselines. Moreover, LLMDPA audits a repository in approximately 50 s, providing a scalable and efficient complement to scale-sensitive attack evaluations. Overall, LLMDPA provides an interpretable and evidence-traceable instantiation of Pre-execution Privacy Auditing for DP-SGD.

Abstract As LLM‐based agents move onto multiagent platforms, they process direct prompts and surrounding social context—posts, comments, and upvotes—an attack surface that single‐turn alignment never addressed. We built a simulation of Moltbook, a social network for AI agents, and a pipeline turning 100 JailBreakBench goals into platform‐native posts with bystander comments of three valences: aggressive, ethical, and measured. Platform‐context reformatting alone raises the attack success rate (ASR) of GPT‐4o‐mini from 7% to 71%, beating a twenty‐query optimization baseline in one pass. Valence then acts as a bidirectional safety modulator: Ethical comments sharply suppress ASR, aggressive endorsements paradoxically reduce it by exposing intent, and measured, intellectually toned comments prove most dangerous, sustaining or elevating ASR. An ablation identifies valence rather than volume as key—a 35‐fold rise in upvotes leaves ASR unchanged—and every finding reproduces under an independent safety classifier with human adjudication. Ambiguous social context thus poses a greater threat than explicit pressure, while safety‐valenced signals offer a deployable defense for agentic platforms.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract Industrial machines are used continuously in many manufacturing environments, so a small fault can quickly affect production, increase maintenance cost, or cause unexpected downtime. Bearing failure is a common example. Before a bearing becomes seriously damaged, the machine may start producing an unusual sound. Finding these changes by manual listening requires experience and regular monitoring. Machine AI was developed to support this task by analyzing machine sounds with artificial intelligence. The system accepts recorded machine audio or a WAV file and uses a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to decide whether the sound represents normal operation or a bearing fault. Industrial audio data, including the MIMII dataset, is used during model development. Librosa and SoundFile are used to prepare the audio, while PyTorch supports the machine-learning model. After the CNN gives a prediction, the result is sent through the Gemini API to a generative-AI module. Gemini prepares a maintenance report with the detected condition, possible causes, severity, and suggested actions. This gives the user more useful information than a fault label alone. The complete application is delivered through HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Flask, with a database for user details, audio-analysis results, predictions, and reports. Overall, Machine AI combines audio analysis, deep learning, and generative AI to support predictive maintenance in a practical web-based system. Keywords Machine Fault Detection, Predictive Maintenance, CNN, Audio Analysis, Deep Learning, Generative AI, Bearing Fault, MIMII

The aim of this work is to evaluate the impacts of heat generation on the radiative flow of Casson nanofluid over a sheet under LTNE circumstances while microbes are present, utilizing machine learning techniques based on the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm. A simple method for moving tiny particles across a temperature gradient is thermophoretic particle deposition, which is essential for electrical and aerosol solution engineering. The energy equations are derived from the local thermal non-equilibrium to determine the unique thermal profiles of the solid and liquid phases. The current model, which combines the Levenberg-Marquardt method with AI-NN (artificial intelligence neural networks), offers a more complex computational solution than standard numerical methods. The proposed model has broad uses in environmental research, and industrial fluid dynamics. By optimizing microorganisms in MHD Casson nanofluid flow with thermophoretic particle deposition, the model improves pollutant removal by bio-convection, leading to better wastewater treatment. It helps in the growth of more efficient bioreactors for microbial fuel cells and pharmaceutical medication delivery systems. Furthermore, nanofluid-based heat transfers and advanced biotechnology applications gain from the capacity to precisely predict and control microbe behaviour in complex fluid environments through the use of ANNs (artificial neural networks). The concentration profile decreases as the thermophoretic parameter values rise.
topics: Heat and Mass Transfer in Porous Media

documents.abstract: Abstract Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related clinical objectives. We further summarize the diverse array of ML architectures currently employed in amyloid research, spanning classical algorithms (e.g., support vector machines and random forests) to advanced deep learning frameworks, such as the transformer framework, protein language models (PLMs), etc. Additionally, we spotlight emerging frontiers, namely, the integration of ML with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, the use of generative AI for de novo inhibitor design, etc., while addressing persistent bottlenecks in the field, including data standardization, model interpretability, and rigorous experimental validation for in silico predictions. Ultimately, this review serves as a foundational roadmap for emerging researchers and a definitive reference for established investigators operating at the intersection of artificial intelligence and amyloid biology.

The main aim of the article is to investigate how translation students interact with AI-generated translations and examines the relationship between AI literacy and post-editing performance. Using a corpus-based mixed-methods approach, the study compares human translation, neural machine translation post-editing, and generative AI post-editing. The findings reveal that generative AI improves fluency and lexical diversity but introduces AI-specific challenges, including hallucinations and contextual distortions. Statistical analysis demonstrates that AI literacy, critical evaluation skills, and prompt formulation abilities significantly influence post-editing quality. The study proposes an AI-enhanced MTPE competence framework integrating linguistic, technological, evaluative, and collaborative dimensions. The results contribute to current discussions on translator competence and provide practical recommendations for translator education in AI-mediated environments. The study employs a mixed-methods research design combining corpus linguistics, quantitative statistical analysis, and qualitative thematic analysis. Data were collected from 60 undergraduate and graduate translation students divided into three groups: Human Translation (HT), Neural Machine Translation Post-Editing (NMTPE), and Generative AI Post-Editing (GAI-PE). The learner corpus consisted of approximately 90,000 words. Translation quality, error frequency, lexical diversity, and AI literacy indicators were analyzed using corpus tools and statistical procedures. The study expands traditional translation competence models by incorporating AI literacy, prompt engineering, hallucination detection, and human–AI collaboration as essential dimensions of MTPE competence. Unlike previous studies focusing mainly on translation quality and productivity, this research examines how AI-related competencies influence student translators' performance in generative AI environments. The findings indicate that generative AI enhances translation fluency and lexical richness while simultaneously creating risks associated with factual inaccuracies and hallucinations. AI literacy emerged as a significant predictor of post-editing performance, highlighting the growing importance of critical evaluation skills in translator training. The study concludes that future translator education should integrate AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical assessment strategies to prepare students for technology-rich professional environments.

Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming modern medicine, providing powerful tools to assist clinicians. However, the most accurate models are opaque, and their limited interpretability hinders clinical adoption and raises regulatory concerns. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) aims to make these models’ decisions comprehensible. Despite its rapid growth and the many reviews already published, aspects such as the rigor of explanation evaluation, clinician involvement, and the use of large language models to generate explanations appear to have received limited attention. This article is a structured, relevance-prioritized review of XAI applied in healthcare, organized around six research questions covering the XAI techniques used, the data and clinical domains they are paired with, the models they explain, how evaluation is performed, the identified limitations, and the use of large language models. Unlike prior reviews that each address only part of this scope, we bring these dimensions together and quantify how rigorously explanations are evaluated and how often the underlying models are externally validated. We conducted a structured search across four literature sources: IEEE Xplore, PubMed, Google Scholar, and PubMed Central (PMC). We adapted the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) flow by carrying a relevance-prioritized subset forward to full-text eligibility assessment, yielding 64 articles for synthesis. Within this corpus, our review revealed a predominantly image-based, post hoc XAI landscape dominated by a few established methods such as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), mostly paired with convolutional, tree-based, and hybrid models on classification and risk-prediction tasks. Clinicians evaluated the explanations in only a minority of the included studies, and relatively few models were externally validated, with no evidence of large language models in our corpus. We conclude that stronger evaluation practices and closer collaboration with clinicians are needed to produce models that are clinically useful and safe to deploy.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of developing preschool children’s cognitive engagement through didactic games. Drawing on international, Russian and Uzbek scholarship, it explores the relationship between educational goals, children’s independent exploration and adult guidance. The statistical section provides a secondary analysis of published meta-analytic findings. Principles are proposed for selecting age-appropriate tasks, gradually increasing the complexity of play and observing children’s cognitive engagement.

This article presents integrative indicators of two types for assessing the effectiveness of management of counteraction to destructive information network influence (DINI). The social factors of the multidimensionality of managerial activity at the meso, macro, and micro levels of society are described, which form the most complete picture of the current situation. The first type of indicators reflects the possibilities for objective assessment of the effectiveness of management of counteraction to DINI at the macro and meso levels of society in the most significant social spheres. The second type of indicators is oriented toward taking into account the significance of the human factor. The validity of the choice is evident in the implementation of the original sociological research program.

The problem of structural labor shortages in the digital economy requires the implementation of breakthrough personnel innovations. Generative AI (GAI), which has automation and cognitive augmentation functions, is considered a strategic tool for managing the transformation of cognitive potential and compensating for labor shortages. The lack of quantitative assessment of the scale of labor shortage compensation through the dual effect (replacement and augmentation) of GAI in key sectors of the economy and the need to verify the strategic role of GAI as a personnel innovation are driving research on this issue. An assessment was conducted of the management of the transformation of the economy’s cognitive potential through the introduction of AI as a personnel innovation in conditions of a labour shortage. A comprehensive approach was applied, combining general scientific methods, statistical analysis, and economic mathematical modelling. The overall compensation of cognitive load through the implementation of generative AI in trade, manufacturing, and professional activities will amount to 5.752 million people in terms of headcount equivalent by 2027, which is more than four times the projected need to compensate for the structural deficit (1.4 million people). Generative AI acts not only as a means of covering the staffing deficit but also as a tool for the qualitative transformation of the economy’s cognitive potential, shifting the focus of employment to hybrid jobs and tasks that require a “human core” of competencies. For the first time, the concept of the “cognitive substitutability coefficient of GAI” (λGAI) has been proposed within the framework of the model of cognitive transformation of labor resources to quantitatively assess the total compensatory effect (automation + augmentation) of implementing GAI in the economy.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: The demand for quality graduates from Vocational High Schools (SMK) faces substantial challenges, notably institutional governance gaps and the weak integration of industrial values. This disparity reveals that vocational education governance has not been fully anchored in functionally integrated work culture cultivation. Consequently, this study aims to analyze school culture management in strengthening educational governance in the Industrial Mechanical Engineering (TMI) Expertise Program at SMK Cibitung 1 through planning, organizing, actuating, and controlling phases. A qualitative approach with a case study design was employed, gathering data through in-depth interviews, participatory observation, and documentation analysis. Data were analyzed interactively utilizing data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. The findings demonstrate that school culture management is systematically executed through POAC functions by integrating religious values, discipline, occupational health and safety (OHS), and the 5S/5R culture. This management model reinforces vocational governance by improving stakeholder participation, coordination transparency, and institutional accountability. The study concludes that the structured internalization of industrial culture serves as a strategic managerial foundation for achieving high-quality vocational education governance. Practical implications highlight the indispensability of formal industrial partnerships and exemplary leadership in institutionalizing a sustainable quality culture within vocational schools. ABSTRAK Tuntutan kualitas lulusan Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan (SMK) menghadapi tantangan serius berupa kesenjangan tata kelola kelembagaan dan rendahnya integrasi nilai-nilai kerja industri. Kesenjangan ini memperlihatkan bahwa tata kelola pendidikan vokasi belum sepenuhnya berlandaskan pada pembudayaan etos kerja yang terintegrasi secara fungsional. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis manajemen budaya sekolah dalam penguatan tata kelola pendidikan pada Program Keahlian Teknik Mekanik Industri (TMI) di SMK Cibitung 1 melalui tahapan perencanaan, pengorganisasian, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi partisipatif, serta analisis dokumentasi. Analisis data dilakukan secara interaktif dengan model kondensasi data, penyajian data, dan verifikasi simpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa manajemen budaya sekolah dilaksanakan secara sistematis melalui fungsi planning, organizing, actuating, dan controlling yang mengintegrasikan nilai religius, kedisiplinan, keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja (K3), serta budaya 5R (Ringkas, Rapi, Resik, Rawat, Rajin). Manajemen budaya sekolah terbukti memperkuat tata kelola pendidikan kejuruan melalui peningkatan partisipasi pemangku kepentingan, transparansi koordinasi, dan akuntabilitas kerja. Simpulan penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa internalisasi budaya industri yang terstruktur merupakan modal manajerial strategis dalam mewujudkan tata kelola kejuruan yang bermutu. Implikasi praktisnya menunjukkan pentingnya kemitraan industri formal dan keteladanan pimpinan dalam melembagakan budaya mutu di lingkungan sekolah kejuruan.

topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence in healthcare has shown great potential over recent decades. In Brazil,this approach follows the expansion of research and academic collaboration in that field. In this regard, thisstudy conducts an exploratory analysis of the scientific production and the collaboration among Brazilianresearchers working on artificial intelligence and machine learning applied to healthcare. A quantitativeapproach was employed, using scriptLattes software to map data from the Lattes platform from 2008 to2024. The analyses covered temporal evolution, geographical distribution, the most recurrent institutions and fields of concentration, keywords, and collaboration networks, assessing trends and gaps in the field. The results demonstrate significant growth in scientific production, concentrated in the Southeast region, and predominance of terms associated with the technologies employed and diagnostic applications, withemphasis on covid-19. Furthermore, the need for greater interdisciplinary and interinstitutional collaboration as well as greater attention to ethics, governance, and regulation is evident.
topics: Diverse Approaches in Healthcare and Education Studies

documents.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to systematically map the vast body of academic literature on student-managed investment funds (SMIFs). It categorizes and indexes the research into a database, allowing scholars and practitioners to efficiently navigate decades of literature based on specific structural and operational characteristics. Design/methodology/approach This study employs an indexing methodology to organize the SMIF literature published between 1975 and 2025, classifying collected papers into three groups: surveys, case studies and general research. Findings The vast majority of SMIF research, 97 out of 126 papers included, are case studies. The index documents SMIF exploration from traditional equity and fixed-income investments into alternative assets such as venture capital and crypto assets and covers recent developments in environmental, social and governance investing and artificial intelligence adoption. Twelve surveys provide SMIF landscape snapshots. Nineteen general research papers discuss a wide range of topics such as challenges, fund performance and experiential learning. Institutions and faculty can use these findings to improve existing programs, while schools planning to start SMIFs can investigate various program structures and fund operation styles. Originality/value This study is the first to use an indexing approach to turn decades of SMIF literature into a structured database, acting as an archival “finding aid.” This preserves the operational details provided by fund insiders (the authors), empowering readers to quickly filter the literature and pinpoint the specific research papers that align with their interests.

The objective was to map the existing scientific, regulatory, and doctrinal evidence on the influence of artificial intelligence on the Ecuadorian judicial system, with an emphasis on its relationship with the protection or possible violation of human rights. The methodology consisted of a scoping review, analyzing 16 articles that met the inclusion and exclusion criteria. The results show the artificial intelligence applications most frequently reported or proposed in the Ecuadorian justice system, the effect of artificial intelligence on human rights, and the risks of its adoption without specific regulations. It concludes that the immediate challenge for the Ecuadorian judicial system is to build a comprehensive legal framework for algorithmic governance, based on international human rights standards, in order to guarantee the transparency, explainability, and institutional accountability of artificial intelligence systems and thus minimize risks to the principles of due process, equality before the law, and effective judicial protection.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Training long-horizon language model agents requires assigning credit to intermediate decisions from sparse terminal feedback. Within a finite group of sibling rollouts, useful action comparisons depend on their context, evidence for both alternatives, and how that evidence enters learning. We propose Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization (MCGPO), a procedure for constructing weighted action preferences from already collected trajectories. MCGPO defines comparison contexts with pre-action state summaries and observed rubric progress, annotated by task rules. Two-action support selects among ordered exact and coarse matching rules. Fixed folds separate candidate decisions from the terminal outcomes used to orient their preferences, and support-dependent evidence weights scale an auxiliary pairwise objective alongside shared GraphGPO task learning. MCGPO reuses rollout data and each response's original history, preserving critic-free training. Across six environment-backbone settings with three training seeds each, MCGPO improves mean success over matched GraphGPO: by 0.47-1.46 percentage points on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B, and by 3.96 and 5.16 points on WebShop with Qwen3-4B and 8B. The ALFWorld gains build on baseline success above 92%, where remaining headroom is limited. Integrated success improves in three of four Qwen2.5 settings. Three-seed factorial controls support opposite-fold evidence and evidence weighting; joint state-rubric matching achieves the highest mean in all four representation-control settings.

This paper introduces MathVis, a benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to visualize frontier mathematical problems and perform diagram-assisted reasoning. The benchmark consists of 512 tasks, each comprising a mathematical statement, a reference diagram, executable TikZ or SVG code, a Gold Intermediate Representation (IR), atomic rubrics, and error codes. Through rigorous evaluation, GPT-6-Astra, Claude Fable 5, and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview achieve pass@1 scores of 31.25%, 26.56%, and 22.85%, respectively. We found that although the tasks require visualization, LLMs produce outputs dominated by formal languages, symbols, and graphics programs, rather than explicit diagram-mediated reasoning. Furthermore, while the solutions generated by LLMs may contain all the necessary elements, they are often visually confusing to humans. Ultimately, this benchmark aims to visualize mathematical problems and promote research on enabling LLMs to simplify their reasoning via visual diagrams.

Eye tracking provides a noninvasive method for measuring visual attention during human-computer interaction. Identifying which oculometric measures are most sensitive to different demands is important for the development of attention-aware systems. This pilot study examined whether common oculometric measures could distinguish between global, selective, and sustained visual attention tasks during low-demand viewing of static images. Ten participants (two males and eight females, 27.5 ± 4.7 years) completed descriptive, comparison-based, and memory-based visual tasks while wearing an eye tracker. Measures included task duration, fixation count, fixation percentage, blink count, blink percentage, and pupil diameter. Repeated-measures analyses showed a marginal effect of task condition on fixation count, with fixation counts descriptively highest during the global attention task and lowest during the selective attention task. Fixation percentage, blink measures, pupil diameter, and task duration did not significantly differ across conditions. These preliminary findings suggest that fixation count may be more sensitive to task-related attentional differences during low-demand visual interaction than blink- or pupil-based measures, supporting its potential use in future attention-aware and multimodal human-computer interaction systems.

Abstract—Foundation models, particularly autoregressive Transformer Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs), have exhibited unprecedented reasoning and generative capabilities across computer science and engineering. However, their internal representations operate as opaque, high-dimensional 'black boxes.' Conventional Explainable AI (XAI) techniques—predominantly post-hoc attribution methods such as Integrated Gradients, SHAP, and attention heatmap visualizations—fail to provide faithful causal explanations: they reflect output correlations rather than the internal mechanistic computations executing within the network, masking hazardous failure modes like latent hallucinations, sycophancy, and deceptive alignment. Mechanistic Interpretability has emerged as a rigorous bottom-up paradigm that seeks to reverse-engineer deep neural networks into human-understandable algorithmic circuits, decomposing polysemantic neuron activations into monosemantic features. This paper provides an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation of mechanistic interpretability and XAI for modern foundation models. We formalize the Linear Representation Hypothesis and the mathematics of neural superposition, analyze transformer residual streams as communicative communication buses, and model the discovery of specialized functional subgraphs—including induction heads, factual recall circuits, and indirect object identification (IOI) subnetworks. Furthermore, we evaluate Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) as an unsupervised mechanism to disentangle polysemantic latent spaces into overcomplete, monosemantic feature dictionaries. Finally, we implement an empirical evaluation testbed across open foundation models (Llama-3-8B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B), quantitatively benchmarking causal scrubbing, activation patching, and SAE feature steering across mission-critical tasks (deceptive alignment detection, factual hallucination suppression, and jailbreak defense). Our findings demonstrate that activation patching isolates causal circuits responsible for 92.4% of factual routing, while SAE-guided feature clamping suppresses unfaithful hallucinations by 41.7% with less than 2.1% degradation in baseline perplexity. We conclude by formulating open challenges in circuit universality, superposition scaling laws, and regulatory verification under international AI governance frameworks. Index Terms—Mechanistic Interpretability, Explainable AI (XAI), Foundation Models, Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), Polysemanticity, Neural Superposition, Induction Heads, Activation Patching, Transformer Circuits.

On-Policy Self-distillation is a self-improvement paradigm that enables large language models (LLMs) to improve their capabilities by leveraging the same model as both teacher and student under different conditioning contexts. However, we find that OPSD methods can progressively degrade previously acquired capabilities: queries that are correctly responded at earlier training stages may become incorrectly responded as optimization proceeds, even the overall performance continues to improve. Further analysis reveals that this degradation coincides with a deterioration of the geometry of hidden representations, characterized by reduced intra-cluster compactness and diminished inter-cluster separation. Motivated by this observation, we propose Representation Geometry Regularization (RGR), which preserves representation geometry during post-training by encouraging compactness within cluster and separation across cluster. RGR can be seamlessly integrated into existing OPSD methods without altering their core optimization procedures. Extensive experiments on multiple OPSD methods and benchmarks show that RGR generally alleviates capability degradation while retaining capability improvements. Our code is available in https://github.com/supermachinelearner/RGR.

This study examines the relationship between mobile Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) literacy and English writing self-efficacy (EWSE) among university students, with AI feedback engagement (AFE) proposed as a mediating mechanism. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 312 university students in China through validated self-report measures. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was employed to test the proposed relationships and mediation effects. The results show that mobile GenAI literacy (MGL) significantly predicts AFE (β = 0.563, p < 0.001) and EWSE (β = 0.182, p = 0.003), while AFE significantly predicts writing self-efficacy (β = 0.478, p < 0.001). AFE partially mediates the relationship between MGL and writing self-efficacy, accounting for approximately 59.6% of the total effect. The model explains 41.2% of the variance in writing self-efficacy. These findings indicate that the educational value of MGL extends beyond technological competence, with active engagement in AI-generated feedback serving as an important mechanism for strengthening writing confidence. The study highlights the importance of pedagogical approaches that promote critical evaluation, reflective use, and meaningful engagement with AI feedback.

Stance detection remains challenging for large language models (LLMs) due to implicit opinions, sarcasm, and context-dependent expressions of stance. Although automatic prompt optimization offers an alternative to fine-tuning without updating model parameters, existing structured approaches are not specifically designed around stance-label semantics and class-specific ambiguities. We introduce MoPrO-SD, a stance-specific prompt optimization framework that decomposes prompts into functional semantic modules and refines them sequentially using LLM-based feedback. We study three refinement strategies: instruction-only optimization (I), instruction with reasoning (I+R), and instruction with per-example reasoning (I+R+E), using class-conditioned errors for stance-label refinement. We also introduce VaccineStance, a new human-annotated benchmark for vaccine stance detection. Experiments across four datasets and five open-weight LLMs show that MoPrO-SD improves upon the human-written Base prompt in many settings. On SemEval-2016, class-conditioned feedback achieves higher mean Macro-F1 than pooled feedback for four of five backbones. Both reasoning-based strategies, I+R and I+R+E, achieve strong performance, with their relative effectiveness varying across models and datasets, while remaining competitive with recent prompt optimization methods. The MoPrO-SD code and VaccineStance dataset are available on GitHub.

The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based maritime surveillance is becoming an important part of maritime Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems. It provides a flexible and cost-effective way to large-scale maritime traffic monitoring. However, achieving robust situational awareness remains challenging in practical maritime environments. The main challenges arise from heterogeneous sensing modalities, adverse imaging conditions, and spatial misalignment caused by UAV motion. To address these problems, this paper proposes an airborne multi-modal graph learning-driven framework, termed AMGT, for vessel identification and tracking in UAV-assisted maritime IoT. Specifically, visible and infrared images are first aligned and fused through a multi-parameter perspective transformation model. This improves visual perception under low visibility and complex illumination conditions. Automatic identification system (AIS) messages are then temporally synchronized using interpolation and linear prediction. To detect small and oriented vessels, we develop a mixed-modality MAir-YOLOv8-OBB detector, followed by the MAir-SORT algorithm for stable vessel tracking. We further design a graph learning-driven association network to model temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies among vessels and between vessels and UAVs. A motion-aware coordinate unification (MCU) strategy is also introduced to reduce nonlinear misalignment caused by UAV motion. Experiments on the MAP-M2UAV50 dataset show that AMGT achieves high accuracy and efficiency. The results demonstrate its potential for UAV-assisted maritime IoT applications, including vessel monitoring, traffic situational awareness, and intelligent maritime transportation services. The dataset and code will be available at https://github.com/MAPGroup/AMGT.

Heritage Building Information Modelling (HBIM) projects face significant challenges, especially in relation to multidisciplinary collaboration and project workflows.This paper examines HBIM work processes, presenting a practical framework to improve HBIM workflows and multidisciplinary collaboration occurring on construction heritage projects. Design/methodology/approachAn initial deductive literature review provides a foundation for the study by identifying thematic HBIM industry challenges.An inductive, interpretivist and qualitative examination of HBIM combines survey questionnaire with case study and in-depth interviews to provide a holistic understanding of the opportunities and challenges confronting practitioners. FindingsFindings indicate that HBIM offers great potential for improving heritage protection, but challenges around data management; human factors; technical issues and training skills remain.A resulting framework for improvement identifies five key outcomes around which improvement depends: team coordination; sharing of knowledge; standards and industry specifications; technical tools and training/education.Recommendations are rooted to case study evidence and practitioner opinion; the paper highlighting the need for further research to refine practices globally. OriginalityThe research makes a contribution to the Heritage Building Information Modelling (HBIM) literature through the focused analysis of project work processes and multidisciplinary collaboration, resulting in an improvement framework for industry.The combination of literature review analysis, survey findings, case study examination and practitioner interviews provides a reliable dataset for the arguments made.

In this work, a deep learning-based multimodal framework for evaluating public engagement with public art is introduced by combining computer vision and behavioral analysis. Existing multimodal models have primarily been applied in domains such as educational settings and behavior analysis, while their application to public art assessment remains limited by challenges in representing subjective human factors, complex behaviors, and interactions across modalities. To address these challenges, the proposed framework employs a Transformer-based architecture to integrate multimodal information and model cross-modal interactions. Image and video inputs representing artworks and participant behaviors, including movement, gaze, and interaction, are processed using 3D convolutional neural networks to extract spatiotemporal features, followed by modality-specific encoding and adaptive fusion using cross-attention. The framework generates outputs related to engagement, emotion recognition, and interaction assessment. For component-level evaluation before real-world public art deployment, the framework was evaluated on three complementary benchmark datasets: NTU RGB+D, Kinetics-700, and AVA (Aesthetic Visual Analysis), representing behavioral, activity recognition, and aesthetic perception tasks. In the classification task, the accuracy obtained was 92.0% and the F1-score of 0.909 for NTU RGB+D, while that of Kinetics-700 was 89.0% and the F1-score of 0.878. The AVA dataset was evaluated using aesthetic-score regression, yielding a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.87. These findings provide component-level evidence of computational effectiveness but do not constitute end-to-end validation in real-world public art settings.

As financial markets become increasingly digital and intelligent, stock-price forecasting has emerged as an important topic in financial engineering, artificial intelligence, and data mining. Stock prices are shaped by firm fundamentals, macroeconomic conditions, investor sentiment, and market policies, while also exhibiting strong nonlinearity, nonstationarity, and noise. Extracting useful information from historical financial data and developing accurate and stable forecasting models therefore remain challenging. This study proposes an improved Transformer for multivariate stock time-series forecasting that combines feature-gated embedding with a residual prediction head. Daily data for Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), and Google (GOOG) were obtained from the public YFinance interface for the period from January 1, 2000, to January 1, 2020. The model uses eight features—Open, High, Low, Close, Volume, RSI, ATR, and MACD—from the previous 30 trading days to predict the closing price five trading days ahead. A strictly chronological split, training-set-only normalization, and separate sliding-window construction are adopted to prevent look-ahead leakage. The proposed model is compared with Persistence, residual XGBoost, LSTM, a vanilla Transformer, and a standard feature-gated Transformer through the main experiment, cross-stock generalization tests, an ablation study, and a supplementary return-prediction experiment. On AAPL, the model achieves an RMSE of 1.2712, an MAE of 0.9242, and a MAPE of 2.5268%, slightly outperforming Persistence and residual XGBoost. It performs nearly identically to Persistence on GOOG and is slightly weaker than Persistence and residual XGBoost on MSFT, while consistently outperforming the LSTM and Transformer-based deep-learning baselines. These results demonstrate the accuracy and stability of the proposed model.

Nanomaterials are increasingly applied in modern agriculture to improve crop productivity, nutrient efficiency, and plant protection through fertilizers, pesticides, and delivery systems. However, their growing implementation raises significant concerns regarding environmental fate, ecological toxicity, and potential risks to human health. This review aims to (i) summarize current knowledge on nanomaterial applications in agriculture and (ii) critically evaluate their associated environmental and health risks. The manuscript integrates evidence on nanoparticle behavior in soil–plant–water systems, including transport, transformation, uptake, and accumulation across trophic levels. Particular attention is given to key toxicity mechanisms such as oxidative stress, membrane damage, genotoxicity, and bioaccumulation across terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. The review also highlights limitations of current studies, which are predominantly short-term and laboratory-based, lacking long-term field validation and standardized risk assessment approaches. Emerging approaches such as artificial intelligence-based optimization and commercial nano-enabled agricultural products, along with existing regulatory frameworks, are further discussed. By integrating agronomic, toxicological, and regulatory perspectives, this review provides a comprehensive systems-level overview of nano-enabled agriculture, emphasizing the urgent need for harmonized risk assessment methodologies, long-term environmental monitoring, and interdisciplinary research.

Background This study examined associations between narcissistic traits and emotional dependence on large language models (LLMs) among adolescents, focusing on anxiety and physical activity. Methods A multistage stratified sample of 1622 Chinese junior high school students was surveyed in November 2025. Narcissistic traits, anxiety, LLM emotional dependence, and physical activity were assessed using the FFNI-SF, GAD-2, an adapted five-item LLM emotional dependence measure, and PARS-3, respectively. Pearson correlations and PROCESS Models 4 and 7 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples were conducted, with Johnson–Neyman analysis used to probe the interaction. Results Narcissistic traits correlated positively with anxiety (r=0.118, P<0.001) and LLM emotional dependence (r=0.301, P<0.001), while anxiety correlated positively with LLM emotional dependence (r=0.146, P<0.001). Physical activity correlated negatively with anxiety (r=−0.119, P<0.001) and LLM emotional dependence (r=−0.075, P = 0.002). Adjusting for grade and left-behind status, anxiety showed a small indirect association between narcissistic traits and LLM emotional dependence (Effect=0.011, 95% CI [0.004, 0.020]). The narcissistic traits × physical activity interaction was significant (β=−0.056, P = 0.015), with the narcissism–anxiety association significant below 0.73 SD of physical activity. The moderated mediation index was not significant (Index=−0.0061, 95% bootstrap CI [−0.0130, 0.0001]). Conclusion Narcissistic traits were positively associated with adolescent LLM emotional dependence, with a small cross-sectional indirect association through anxiety. Physical activity moderated the narcissism–anxiety association, although overall moderated mediation was not supported.
