documents.abstract: Deploying AI agents to combat dishonest communication is an intuitive response to deception in hybrid human-AI societies. However, the efficacy of such interventions in realistic networked settings remains unclear. We study this problem using an evolutionary game-theoretic model of the Deceiver's Game by extending it to structured networks, where agents can adopt deception, truth-telling, and investigation strategies. We introduce committed AI agents (zealots) fixed to either truth-telling or investigative strategies and conduct agent-based simulations across three network topologies. Our key findings are: (1) passive committed truth-telling agents can amplify adaptive deception by creating exploitable honest partners, whereas investigative agents increase adaptive truth-telling in the oscillatory regime; (2) intervention effects are non-monotonic in deployment density because committed agents reshape rather than simply suppress the underlying oscillatory dynamics; and (3) response peaks depend on topology, with sampled scale-free populations showing sharp low-density responses and fully connected populations requiring larger committed fractions. Overall, the results highlight the need to distinguish passive truth-telling from active investigation when using committed agents to influence networked deception dynamics.

Neuromarketing is a multidisciplinary field that aims to better understand consumer behaviour at the intersection of neuroscience and marketing. The current trend in academic literature indicates that strategies should focus not only on technological elements but also on human neurological responses. The evolution of marketing communication towards the integration of social media and artificial intelligence technologies requires learning the mechanisms underlying social media behaviour. Social media interactions affect the brain's reward system, while the excessive data density in digital media increases cognitive load, and artificial intelligence-supported algorithms reinforce cognitive biases. Neuromarketing tools integrated with artificial intelligence will facilitate the development of personalised and real-time marketing strategies by analysing subconscious processes more quickly and easily.

Abstract Safe water management requires rapid and highly sensitive analytical platforms capable of detecting contaminants in complex environmental matrices. Nanozymes are nanomaterials with enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity that offer remarkable advantages for field-deployable sensing, including stability and compatibility with portable formats. However, conventional nanozyme sensors often exhibit nonlinear catalytic behavior, limited selectivity, and susceptibility to interference in natural waters. This Perspective evaluates how integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with nanozyme-based systems can resolve these constraints. We analyze mechanistic nanozyme responses to major pollutant classes, including heavy metals, dyes, pharmaceuticals, and pesticides, and show how machine learning and deep learning models enhance sensitivity, mitigate matrix effects, and enable multiplex classification via catalytic fingerprints. We further highlight emerging AI-enabled architectures, including smartphone analytics, Internet of Things (IoT)-based nanozyme devices, and cloud-connected autonomous monitoring systems. Finally, we discuss the potential of standardized datasets, digital-twin simulations, and AI-driven design of single-atom nanozymes to advance global water quality assessment.

Large Language Model agents have made it possibleto talk with digital tools using everyday language but creatingsystems that are dependable and safe requires good organizationof models, integration of tools in parts and careful control ofhow the system runs. This paper introduces NEXUS, a personalproductivity agent that uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP)to carry out tasks that need steps through natural-languageconversation. NEXUS uses Google Gemini as its LLM anduses Groq-hosted Llama 3.3 70B as a backup model givinga second way to think when the main model fails. NEXUSfollows a Think–Act–Observe routine: first NEXUS reads theuser’s request then NEXUS decides what action is needed thenNEXUS asks the tool via MCP then NEXUS checks the outcomeand finally NEXUS writes the response. NEXUS works withFilesystem, To-Do and Web Search MCP services. The customTo-Do service stores task data in SQLite lets users manage taskskeeps a log of changes and allows undo actions. NEXUS also hasa Human-in-the-Loop feature that asks the user to confirm beforeany change that alters the system state is carried out. NEXUScan also start tasks on its own. Can communicate with outsidesystems through its built-in services. By keeping the thinking partof the LLM separate, from the tool actions and by using modelbackup and strict tool controls NEXUS offers a system that’smodular, dependable and able to grow for personal productivity.

documents.abstract: Background: Burnout is prevalent among postgraduate medical trainees, yet stage-stratified data in obstetrics and gynecology (Ob-Gyn) residency remain sparse. The relationship between burnout domains and academic motivation has not been examined in this population. Objectives: To map burnout prevalence and domain severity across four stages of an Ob-Gyn residency program and examine associations between burnout domains and academic motivation subtypes. Methods: This cross-sectional study enrolled 94 Ob-Gyn residents (semesters 2–9) from the Faculty of Medicine, Universitas Airlangga, undergoing clinical training at a major tertiary teaching hospital in Surabaya, Indonesia. Instruments included the Maslach-Trisni Burnout Inventory and Academic Motivation Scale. Results: Overall burnout prevalence was 25.5%, varying markedly across stages: 44.0% (Stage I), 28.0% (Stage II), 7.4% (Stage III), and 23.5% (Stage IV) (p=0.026), forming a non-linear, U-shaped trajectory. Stage I exhibited significantly higher emotional exhaustion than Stage III (p=0.033). Personal accomplishment (PA) positively correlated with all intrinsic motivation subtypes and introjected/identified regulation and negatively with amotivation (p<0.05). External regulation declined from Stage I to IV (p=0.032), independently of burnout. Conclusions: Burnout concentrates at early and late training stages rather than accumulating uniformly. PA co-occurs with autonomous motivation, suggesting a protective resource-like role. Stage-specific interventions and reinforcement of residents’ clinical competence are warranted.

Discourse particles subtly shape the flow of discourse by reflecting conversational context and interlocutor attitudes, often leaving the truth-conditional meaning untouched. They are also often polyfunctional, with distinct senses which partially overlap with other particles; for example, the exclusive use of English "just" and "only" ("John only/just drinks water"). Despite the frequency of these words in natural language, they have gone largely unstudied due to the subtle nature of their effects. We investigate LLM sensitivity to "just" and "only" in natural conversations using behavioral and mechanistic analyses. First, we find that LLMs and humans similarly prefer the presence of these particles in context, and both are more sensitive to "just" compared to "only". Second, when sampling from LLMs with and without these particles, we find LLMs consistently rate generations as more likely, given their source context, demonstrating their particle sensitivity. In both experiments, instruction tuning increases sensitivity. Finally, we localize particle-sensitive units within LLMs and find the overlap between "just" and "only" is asymmetric: "only" units transfer selectively to exclusive "just", while all "just" units transfer to "only" equally well regardless of sense, suggesting LLM lexical-level particle representations are partially organized by sense. We release our code, sense-labeled dialogue stimuli, and human preference annotations at https://github.com/JiahuiKChen/Not_Just_an_Evaluation.

PURPOSE: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have the potential to enhance the delivery of speech-language pathology services. One area of practice that could benefit from AI is automated screenings for developmental language disorder (DLD) in early elementary students. This report presents the elements and processes involved in evaluating an AI-based automated scoring system using archival recordings. METHOD: A total of 947 audio samples of children completing the Redmond Sentence Recall (RSR) task, representing cases with and without DLD, were used. We developed an automated version of the RSR (AutoRSR), employing automated speech recognition (ASR), natural language processing, and machine learning models, to automate the tasks of transcribing recordings, tracking the number of errors children produced, scoring production accuracies based on RSR criteria, and generating pass/fail decisions based on age-referenced expectations against a reference standard (i.e., Core Language scores from the Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals-Fourth Edition for a subset of 130 children). Different speech recognition models (Whisper and Reverb ASR) were applied to examine potential trade-offs. The accuracy of the AutoRSR was compared to human scoring. RESULTS: AutoRSR with Whisper speech recognition yielded sensitivity = .768 and specificity = .784, whereas Reverb speech recognition yielded sensitivity = .873 and specificity = .730. While AutoRSR had some mismatches with human evaluators and tended to produce lower scores, it converged more closely with the reference standard than human-scored protocols. CONCLUSIONS: AI technologies have become powerful enough to automate the scoring of recordings of children's sentence recall with similar accuracy levels as human evaluators. Next steps are discussed. SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34050876.

PURPOSE: Children with developmental language disorder (DLD) produce more speech disruptions and have a slower speech rate than their peers. This study validated measures of effortful sentence production by examining their association with general language ability and differences between groups of children with DLD and typical language development (TLD). Measures of effort were expected to be related to general language ability, and children with DLD were expected to produce more stall-type disruptions (i.e., repetitions, filled pauses, and unfilled pauses) and use fewer words per minute (WPM) than their peers with TLD. METHOD: = 90.64 months) were transcribed, aligned to the audio, and coded for sentence disruptions using the Codes for the Human Analysis of Transcripts form from TalkBank. A custom-made Python script computed measures of stall rate, nondisrupted rate (e.g., the percentage of utterances with no disruptions), and WPM and were examined relative to child performance on the Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals-Fourth Edition. RESULTS: When controlling for age, stall rate and nondisrupted rate were moderately correlated with general language ability, and WPM was strongly correlated with general language ability. The DLD group used significantly more stalls and fewer WPM and nondisrupted utterances than did the TLD group. CONCLUSIONS: The findings demonstrate that measures of effortful sentence production are systematically associated with language ability. Future directions for leveraging artificial intelligence to automate these measures and exploring their utility as value-added indicators of DLD are discussed.

Background: Digital communication tools change how hospital staff request services and follow up patients’ needs. Their value depends on how well they fit everyday work. Women over 40 may bring experience of successive technological changes, but age alone says little about professional seniority or digital confidence. Objective: To understand how Brazilian nurses over 40 perceive the effects of a digital interaction tool on their nursing work. Design: Secondary qualitative analysis informed by Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis. Setting: A large hospital in São Paulo, Brazil. Participants: Ten Brazilian female nurses aged 41–55, selected from 20 interviews on the basis of age and explicitly recorded female identification. One additional interview requires eligibility confirmation. Methods: A second review of a pool of participants followed Braun & Clarke’s six thematic analysis phases: familiarization with data, generating initial codes, searching for themes, reviewing themes, defining and naming themes, and writing the report. Results: Four themes were developed: learning again without starting from scratch; no longer the go-between for every request; when a digital request still needs a phone call; and making work visible without losing personal contact. Participants described easier communication and greater team autonomy, alongside the effort of learning another system, duplicated requests and dependence on other departments’ responses. Comparisons with telephone communication and replacement platforms showed how they assessed successive changes in their working practices. Conclusions: Participants valued the tool when it reduced the need to relay requests and helped them organize care. Its usefulness diminished when they still had to telephone, repeat information or chase a response. Continuing support, integration between systems and clear departmental responsibilities warrant attention. These accounts do not establish an objective reduction in workload or effects specific to age or gender. The analysis remains subject to the research team’s reflexive review.

Understanding the relationship between dietary compounds and epigenetic mechanisms is central to research in nutrigenomics and human health. Structured datasets that systematically integrate dietary, molecular, and epigenetic information are essential for reproducible and data-driven investigation in this domain. This dataset compiles curated associations between 653 unique dietary compounds, 585 food sources, and 80 epigenetic targets, extracted from 1,963 primary research articles identified through systematic searches in PubMed and Web of Science. Compound identification was performed via large language model-assisted extraction and subsequently standardized using PubChem, RDKit, and semantic clustering procedures. Binding affinity data were incorporated for human proteins with validated epigenetic function, prioritizing records with quantitative measures. Variables are harmonized and annotated using recognized chemical and biological ontologies. This resource supports research on nutriepigenomics, compound–mechanism associations, and food-derived bioactives, enabling hypothesis generation, validation studies, and data mining in nutritional, biomedical, and computational research contexts.

This article examines the key factors involved in developing psychological readiness for career choice in late adolescents. Career choice is considered a complex psychological process closely associated with personal interests, abilities, values, motives, self-assessment, and perceptions of future Zamonaviy jamiyat va innovatsiyalar ilmiy nazariy jurnali 2026-yil, 9-Son, 2-Qism. ISSN 3060-544X professional development. Career orientation, intrinsic motivation, self-awareness, adequate self- evaluation, decision-making ability, stability of professional interests, and reflective readiness are identified as essential components of psychological readiness for career choice. Particular attention is given to the influence of the family environment, pedagogical support, peers, access to career-related information, and the broader social context on professional self-determination. The article emphasizes that awareness of the correspondence between an individual’s psychological characteristics and the requirements of a chosen profession is an important prerequisite for conscious and sustainable career decision-making. Motivational, cognitive, personal-reflective, and socio-psychological factors are interpreted as interconnected components of a unified system that supports effective professional self- determination in late adolescence.

Injuries and occupational diseases represent an important economic factor in different industrial sectors. In Italy alone, there have been over 60000 confirmed cases of occupational diseases in 2022, where musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) represent 70% of the total. This fact highlights the importance of protecting workers against physical efforts. While current ergonomic tools can mitigate most of the risk factors, there is still a non-negligible number of tasks that cannot be completely compensated for. This is due to the high complexity and costs of the workplace reorganization, or simply strict requirements of the target task. In some of these cases, exoskeletons are a viable solution. This chapter introduces different kinds of existing exoskeletons, with particular focus on occupational exoskeletons, considering commercial systems already deployed in industry, and some of the most promising technologies which will arrive in the next years. The deployment of occupational exoskeletons is conditioned by the regulatory frameworks and by the required reorganization of the workplace. Both concepts and the latest developments are discussed in this chapter, including their integration into Industry 4.0. Finally, this chapter describes the most common evaluation methods and discusses current efforts toward standardized benchmarking methods which will allow evaluating the benefit of using exoskeletons in real applications.

Gas station employees are chronically exposed to fuel vapors containing benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene (BTEX), and other volatile organic compounds (VOCs), raising occupational concerns about olfactory function. In this cross-sectional study, 116 Brazilian gas station employees (86 men and 30 women; median age, 37.5 years; range, 19–58) completed a questionnaire and underwent objective olfactory assessment with the MultiScent-20 digital odor identification test. Overall, 58.6% had olfactory dysfunction, including 46.6% with hyposmia and 12.1% with anosmia, whereas only 23.3% reported that their work affected their sense of smell. Longer employment duration was associated with lower olfactory scores (Spearman's ρ = −0.41; p < 0.001) and independently increased the odds of dysfunction (odds ratio [OR] = 1.15 per additional year; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06–1.26; p = 0.003). These findings support incorporating olfactory assessment into occupational health surveillance for workers chronically exposed to fuel vapors.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: The increasing capability of large language models (LLMs) creates an opportunity to redesign how users interact with computational design software. Architectural planning is a particularly relevant domain because early-stage requirements are often expressed in natural language, while the resulting design must ultimately be represented as geometry. This paper presents Omni Build Intelligence, an implemented full-stack prototype that explores an LLM-assisted workflow for generating preliminary architectural floor plans from structured user requirements. The system accepts building type, requested room count, plot width and length, and special requirements. A Flask backend constructs a domain-specific prompt and invokes a Llama 3.3 70B model through the Grok API. The response is expected in a structured textual format containing rooms, coordinates, dimensions, door relationships, and a summary. The generated representation is parsed into easy for software to read objects and passed to a React interface. The interface provides a two-dimensional blueprint view and an isometric three-dimensional visualization. A conversion layer transforms generated room rectangles into editable wall and label primitives that can be associated with a project record. The broader platform also includes authentication, project management, plot listing and filtering, dashboard functionality, and persistence of drawing data. These components make Omni Build more than a standalone text-generation demonstration: it is a prototype for integrating generative AI into an interactive design workflow. The research contribution of this paper is the formulation of a rigorous evaluation methodology for such a system. The proposed methodology defines an Architectural Requirement Prompt Dataset, meaningful baselines, formal geometric constraints, automated validation metrics, human evaluation criteria, ablation experiments, and statistical analysis procedures. Metrics include constraint satisfaction, boundary violations, room overlap, requirement accuracy, dimension validity, space use of space, valid-plan rate, and generation latency. A user guided study is proposed to evaluate perceived practicality and usefulness. The study deliberately does not claim measured superiority because the repository provides implementation evidence but not a completed controlled benchmark. Instead, the paper establishes a reproducible experimental framework through which the system can be evaluated. This distinction prevents software functionality from being mistaken for research evidence. The work concludes that LLM-based architectural assistance is most appropriately positioned as an early-stage design aid whose natural-language flexibility is combined with explicit geometric validation and human review. Keywords: large language models, generative AI, computer based architectural design, floor-plan generation, constraint based prompting, spatial reasoning, structured generation, user guided design, interactive visualization, project management

An AI agent receives permission to execute a command. But what if the command reaches the wrong destination, the payment follows a compromised route, or a robotic actuator behaves differently from what was authorized? Should that original permission still allow the system to continue? As frontier AI models and autonomous agents increasingly control financial transactions, cloud infrastructure, sensitive communications, software deployments, industrial equipment, robotics, and critical systems, conventional authorization faces a fundamental limitation: permission to execute does not establish that the intended real-world effect actually occurred. This paper examines a different approach to machine authority: “A permit to effect once is not a permit to effect permanently.” Building on the principle that “Computation is not authority to act,” the proposed architecture introduces a further requirement: authority to continue must be earned through independently verified evidence of a preceding real effect. The paper presents a safety-first execution-finality architecture based on Receipt-Gated Interim Effectuation Validation (IEV). Instead of immediately releasing the full consequence of a high-risk operation, the system can authorize a deliberately bounded real effect on the actual operational path. A protected observer, destination, transaction system, network component, or hardware controller produces evidence of what actually occurred. An independent Interim Effectuation Validator examines that evidence against the authorized act, expected outcome, destination, scope, freshness, policy, and revocation state. Only successful validation establishes the protected continuation condition required for the next phase. In stronger realizations, this is not merely another software approval. The cryptographic material required to complete the next effect is unavailable until the preceding real-world effect has been independently verified. Continuation may depend on receipt-bound key derivation, split credentials, protected state transitions, threshold approvals, hardware registers, or other protected enforcement mechanisms. The validator does not relay the original command, and an agent's own assertion of success is never a substitute for required independent evidence. The paper consolidates 35 execution-finality workflow profiles (E01–E35) spanning eight broad technical families, including: AI agents, autonomous tool execution, frontier model deployment, and credential control. Financial transactions, payment verification, settlement, and protected value release. Messages, file transfers, confidential data disclosure, and destination verification. Cloud infrastructure, database mutations, software updates, and persistent AI memory. Robotics, industrial automation, autonomous vehicles, and unmanned aerial systems. Telecommunications, radio transmission, satellite operations, and network control. GPUs, accelerators, hardware enforcement, and protected execution domains. Distributed effectuation, quorum validation, uncertain outcomes, and recovery. The architecture also examines 12 implementation-equivalence and design-around closures, addressing attempts to bypass the protected causal dependency through alternate execution paths, substituted components, software–hardware rearrangements, or different credential and validation topologies. A dedicated Safety-First Critical-System Profile establishes that execution correctness, consequence containment, and mandatory validation take precedence over minimizing latency. Optimizations remain possible, but they must preserve the protections selected for the relevant consequence class. A further distinction is made between simulation and actual effectuation. A successful simulation cannot establish that the real recipient, network route, transaction destination, or physical actuator will behave as expected. The proposed staged mechanism therefore uses bounded effects on the actual consequence-capable path, subject to protected observation and explicit safety assumptions. When evidence is missing, conflicting, stale, replayed, or indeterminate, ordinary continuation remains unavailable. Unknown outcomes require reconciliation, bounded remediation, safe-state handling, or protected escalation—not automatic success or blind retry. The central research question is straightforward: Should a high-consequence autonomous machine be permitted to cause its next irreversible effect before independently verifying what happened during its previous authorized effect? This publication proposes that, for selected high-risk operations, real-world evidence should become a technical and cryptographic prerequisite for continuing execution—not merely an audit record produced after the consequences have occurred. The paper is a technical architecture and analytical contribution. It does not report experimental deployment, measured security improvements, or empirical validation. Its proposed properties depend on assumptions concerning evidence integrity, protected authority, enforcement-path completeness, and atomic consumption of continuation authority. Patent pending: Indian Patent Office application 202631117633, “Systems and Methods for Cryptographically Staged Effectuation with Verified Partial Effect, Receipt-Bound Full Effectuation, and Software-Hardware Enforcement.” This publication makes no assertion that any particular commercial system implements the architecture and does not establish patentability, infringement, ownership, or priority. Invitation for Independent Technical Review Researchers, frontier AI model providers, cloud and hardware engineers, security architects, patent professionals, and critical-infrastructure specialists are invited to examine the 35 workflows, test the security assumptions, identify relevant prior art, challenge the anti-bypass properties, and evaluate whether receipt-dependent execution authority provides meaningful additional protection for consequential autonomous systems. Critical feedback, adversarial analysis, alternative engineering approaches, and independent conclusions are welcome.

Time series causal discovery --- the process of detecting causation between time series --- has its roots in signal processing research from over a half century ago. It has since received active and widespread interest, evolving into different forms across domains such as statistics, dynamical systems and machine learning. Entering this fragmented and constantly evolving research landscape can be daunting. This tutorial provides a unified overview of time series causal discovery across research communities. We introduce the key principles invoked by modern discovery methods, and we discuss their limitations and assumptions. We also discuss how discovery methods are evaluated, benchmarked and fine-tuned. We further discuss how causal discovery for time series is becoming crucial for downstream tasks in agriculture and Earth science, in healthcare, and in artificial intelligence systems. We believe that this tutorial will serve as a valuable resource in navigating the deluge of recent causality research, as well as an invitation to signal processing audiences to contribute to causal problems. To further help readers, we host a companion repository to link to useful code packages and resources at https://github.com/CHAI-UK/Awesome-Time-Series-Causal-Discovery.
topics: Complex Systems and Time Series Analysis

documents.abstract: Crypto-asset disputes create distinctive barriers to effective remedies because they combine technical opacity, cross-border legal fragmentation, pseudonymous actors, irreversible transactions and uncertain enforcement pathways. These barriers are especially significant for vulnerable and non-expert users, who may be unable to identify the legally relevant harm, organize blockchain-based evidence, select an appropriate forum or obtain practical enforcement. This article develops a conceptual, normative and legal-design proposal for a hybrid Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) architecture that integrates off-chain artificial intelligence (AI) assistance with a minimized on-chain smart-contract layer. The model assigns AI systems a supporting role in legal information, triage, claim classification, evidence organization, explanation and negotiation, while reserving contested legal determinations for human review. A permissioned distributed ledger records only hashes, timestamps, procedural events, escrow states and execution proofs; personal data, communications, evidence and AI processing remain off-chain. Smart contracts are used as bounded enforcement tools for registration, escrow and execution of validated settlement terms, rather than as autonomous adjudicators. The article applies the architecture to three illustrative scenarios: asset seizure and recovery, exchange failure and mass claims, and crypto scams involving cross-border fraud. It then evaluates the model against European requirements concerning artificial intelligence, crypto-asset services, data protection, procedural fairness, cybersecurity and accountability. The contribution is twofold. First, it advances the concept of access to remedies by design, under which comprehension, participation, contestability, evidentiary integrity and enforceability are embedded into the architecture of digital dispute resolution. Second, it provides a technically specified evaluation framework for future prototyping and empirical validation. The article does not claim measured improvements in accessibility or efficiency; rather, it identifies testable design requirements and performance indicators for subsequent pilots, user studies and regulatory sandboxes.

Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with web technologies is one of the most significant areas of development in modern e-commerce systems. AI can substantially improve the processes of designing and building web applications. Modern AI tools can support user interface design, software development and testing, security analysis, and threat detection. This article examines opportunities for using AI in the development of e-commerce web applications and throughout their entire lifecycle, as well as contemporary architectural models, the role of generative AI, and areas of practical application.

The advancement of technological disruption in the digital era necessitates fundamental transformations within vocational education, particularly regarding teachers' readiness to produce innovative and contextual learning materials. Preliminary observations at SMK PGRI 1 Jakarta revealed that only 13.33% of teachers had independently developed interactive digital teaching materials due to technological barriers and time constraints. This Community Service (PkM) initiative aimed to enhance teachers' digital pedagogical competencies through a structured workshop focusing on the development of digital learning materials grounded in a deep learning approach assisted by artificial intelligence (AI) tools. The execution methodology incorporated the Asset-Based Community Development (ABCD) framework synthesized with the procedural phases of the Plomp model, encompassing preliminary research, development/prototyping, and assessment phases. The intervention was conducted offline on June 13, 2026, involving 30 vocational teachers from four expertise concentrations. Data were collected using self-evaluations, expert reviews, one-to-one evaluations, small-group evaluations, and final portfolio assessments. The evaluation results demonstrated that the digital teaching modules achieved an expert validity score of 4.40 out of 5.00 (highly valid), a small-group practicality score of 4.43 out of 5.00 (highly practical), and 86.67% of teachers successfully generated functional digital materials fulfilling vocational curriculum standards. This program offers practical implications as a sustainable instructional mentoring model to cultivate an autonomous digital learning ecosystem in vocational schools. ABSTRAK Perkembangan disrupsi teknologi di era digital menuntut transformasi mendasar pada sektor pendidikan vokasi, khususnya kesiapan guru dalam memproduksi materi pembelajaran yang inovatif dan kontekstual. Berdasarkan studi pendahuluan di SMK PGRI 1 Jakarta, ditemukan bahwa hanya 13,33% guru yang pernah mengembangkan bahan ajar digital interaktif secara mandiri akibat kendala literasi teknologi dan keterbatasan waktu. Program Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kompetensi pedagogik digital guru melalui workshop terstruktur penyusunan bahan ajar digital berbasis pendekatan pembelajaran mendalam (deep learning) berbantuan perangkat kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence / AI). Metode pelaksanaan mengadopsi pendekatan Asset-Based Community Development (ABCD) yang dipadukan dengan siklus pengembangan model Plomp, meliputi fase pengkajian awal (preliminary research), fase perancangan (development or prototyping phase), dan fase penilaian (assessment phase). Kegiatan dilaksanakan secara luring pada tanggal 13 Juni 2026 yang diikuti oleh 30 orang guru kejuruan dari empat konsentrasi keahlian. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan teknik self-evaluation, expert review, one-to-one evaluation, small group evaluation, serta penilaian portofolio produk akhir. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa modul bahan ajar digital yang dikembangkan memperoleh skor validitas ahli sebesar 4,40 dari skala 5,00 (kategori sangat valid), tingkat kepraktisan kelompok sebesar 4,43 dari skala 5,00 (kategori sangat praktis), dan sebanyak 86,67% guru berhasil memproduksi bahan ajar digital siap pakai yang memenuhi kriteria kelayakan kurikulum vokasi. Program ini berimplikasi sebagai model pendampingan instruksional berkelanjutan dalam membangun ekosistem digital mandiri di sekolah kejuruan.

A go-kart is a small, lightweight four-wheeled vehicle designed for recreational, educational and competitive driving. This project deals with the design and fabrication of a go-kart powered by an internal combustion (IC) engine. The main objective is to develop a simple, strong, economical and serviceable vehicle using commonly available mechanical components and workshop processes. The project covers the selection of the IC engine, chassis design, steering system, braking system, power transmission, wheels and tyres, accelerator and control mechanism. The frame is designed to support the engine, driver and other components while maintaining adequate rigidity and stability. The engine converts the chemical energy of fuel into mechanical power, which is transmitted to the driving axle through a suitable transmission arrangement. The methodology includes requirement identification, conceptual design, component selection, basic engineering calculations, CAD/drawing preparation, material procurement, fabrication, assembly and testing. The report also discusses important safety aspects such as braking performance, steering response, chain guarding, fastener tightening and driver protection. The project provides practical understanding of automobile engineering, IC engines, manufacturing processes, machine design, welding, power transmission and vehicle testing. The final design can be further improved by reducing weight, improving ergonomics, optimizing power transmission and introducing additional safety and instrumentation.

The chapter introduces the organizational dimension of ergonomics for robotics. Specifically, it introduces the foundations of organizational ergonomics and sociotechnical principles for effective work systems design and development. It then highlights key challenges involved in issues related to work, activities, and quality of life in robotic setups. In this realm, attitudes towards robots and automation play a major role in the adoption of new technologies and change management in organizations. These broad-scale changes are important to be recognized as they shape human–robot interaction in various work settings, ranging from smart manufacturing to defence. The chapter then addresses specific aspects of teamwork and the design of high-performance teams. These topics include team performance and well-being, human function allocation, shared situation awareness, and job roles, amongst other such topics that will be explored later in the book by subsequent chapters. This chapter supplements the previous chapters on physical and cognitive ergonomics, but it goes beyond these aspects to highlight the organizational basis required to develop robotics holistically.

Post-training has become a key stage for eliciting reasoning capabilities in Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs). Existing post-training methods mainly follow two paradigms: reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). However, they do not fully exploit visual evidence for effective training. RL supervises the policy with a single trajectory-level reward, which is too coarse-grained for video reasoning: the same response-level advantage is applied to every generated token, disregarding that the tokens of a video response are grounded in the visual stream to very different degrees. OPD provides token-level supervision through output-distribution matching, but lacks direct supervision of the spatiotemporal representations that produce those outputs. We observe across extensive experiments that the same model reasons more accurately when its video view combines global temporal context with question-relevant details. Comparing the same student-generated response under this view and uniform sampling reveals changes in token likelihoods and internal representations, providing a training signal for evidence use. Building on this observation, we propose OWLET, an evidence-privileged RL method that derives training signals from a richer teacher view. This view couples uniform global context with question-conditioned local windows, providing visual evidence without requiring a larger model. To better exploit this privileged visual evidence, OWLET introduces (i) \textbf{evidence-aware credit redistribution}, which compares token likelihoods across the two views and redistributes positive response-level advantages according to their relative evidence support; and (ii) \textbf{spatiotemporal state alignment}, which aligns the two views' hidden states on verifier-accepted responses.

documents.abstract: Abstract Plumbers face several occupational health and safety (OHS) risks in the construction industry. However, existing evidence is largely fragmented, dated, or limited to prevalence-based assessments. This study addresses this gap by analyzing recent long-term (15 years, 2009–2023) workers’ compensation data from the Australian construction sector to examine the prevalence, severity, and mechanisms of both physical injuries and occupational diseases among plumbers. Descriptive statistical and two-way and three-way chi-square contingency analyses were performed to examine how incident severity varies across injury and disease types, incident mechanisms and agencies, affected body parts, worker demographics, and organizational size. The study found that physical injuries accounted for 80% of all incidents, and musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and noise-induced hearing loss dominated health issues. Fatalities were primarily linked to asbestos-related diseases and electrocution, and permanent incapacities were driven by hearing loss, MSDs, and amputations. Plumbers accounted for nearly 10% of all construction incidents, with micro-businesses disproportionately affected, and apprentices represented 13% of cases. Noise-induced hearing loss emerged as the leading cause of permanent incapacity, highlighting underrecognized auditory risks. The study also identified 20 most common incident agencies and found strong associations between injury severity and affected body parts, particularly the head, neck, ears, back, shoulders, fingers, and knees. These findings advocate a trade-specific, priority-driven OHS risk management approach, accompanied by changes to policies and management practices related to noise exposure, ergonomic risks, hazardous material handling, and work organization in small enterprises.

documents.abstract: Motivated by the success of large language models (LLMs) with broad generalizability and robustness to noisy or unreliable pre-training data, we explore in-context prediction of PDE solution fields using approximate pre-training data. In addition, inspired by the posterior predictive mean-based inference mechanism of the in-context learning in prior-data fitted networks (PFNs), we propose PDE-PFN, a prior-data fitted neural solver that approximates the posterior predictive mean of PDE solutions via in-context learning. PDE-PFN builds on a PFN architecture with self- and cross-attention mechanisms of Transformer and is pre-trained on noisy approximate solutions generated by physics-informed neural networks, serving as diverse but not necessarily exact priors. Through experiments on a range of two-dimensional PDEs, we demonstrate that PDE-PFN achieves empirical generalization across heterogeneous equations, robustness under noisy priors, and zero-gradient-update in-context inference capability. PDE-PFN achieves competitive or improved predictive accuracy relative to the evaluated baselines while supporting flexible context and query representations.

Utilization of ultra-high-field (UHF) MRI in humans has rapidly increased over the past decade, following regulatory approval of the first clinical 7 Tesla (7T) platforms in 2017 for brain and knee imaging. Currently, there are approximately 140 MRI scanners worldwide operating at or above 7T [1]. While the majority of 7T scanners are dedicated to research and development, select hospitals have successfully implemented 7T MRI for clinical care. Key advantages of 7T over lower-field systems include higher spatial and contrast resolution for anatomic and microstructural detail, susceptibility effects for functional and vascular imaging, and spectral resolution for metabolic evaluation. However, safety considerations-particularly specific absorption rate thresholds-have historically constrained utility to patients with weights of 30 kg and above. Additional considerations, including operating costs, longer imaging times, increased artifacts, and greater bioeffects, have limited widespread adoption, especially in pediatric patients. In this article, we discuss emerging technology advances and clinical applications for 7T MRI imaging of children. Major technical considerations are scanner hardware, coils, safety, sedation, and monitoring. Important clinical applications include neurodevelopmental, epilepsy, demyelinating, vascular, genetic, neoplastic, and traumatic disorders. Major research areas involve artificial intelligence, extracranial imaging, and field strengths exceeding 10T. Real-life imaging examples are provided for children and young adults to highlight the advantages and pitfalls of 7T in this population.

This study was motivated by students’ low proficiency in writing German texts, particularly in grammar use and story development. Meta AI, as an Artificial Intelligence-based technology, can be utilized as a tool to address these challenges. This study aims to (1) measure differences in students’ German writing skills before and after using Meta AI and (2) determine the extent to which Meta AI can help improve students’ German writing skills. This study employed a quantitative approach using a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design. The participants were students enrolled in the Schriftliche Kommunikation course at Universitas Negeri Malang, who were divided into an experimental group and a control group. Data were collected through essay tests, writing assignments, and questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics, a t-test, and Cohen’s d effect size. The results showed that students’ writing skills in the experimental group increased by 10.7 points after using Meta AI. The statistical analysis showed a significant difference in students’ writing skills before and after the treatment, with a p-value of p = 0.003 < 0.05, and Cohen’s d = 0.968, indicating a large effect. The writing assignments and questionnaire results indicated that Meta AI helped students develop ideas, enrich their vocabulary, understand the use of articles (der, die, and das), improve grammatical accuracy, and produce more structured texts. Therefore, Meta AI can serve as a supportive technology that provides gradual assistance in the German writing learning process. ABSTRAK Studi ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya kemampuan mahasiswa dalam menulis teks bahasa Jerman, khususnya dalam penggunaan tata bahasa dan penyusunan alur cerita. Meta AI sebagai teknologi berbasis Artificial Intelligence dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai alat bantu dalam mengatasi permasalahan tersebut. Studi ini bertujuan untuk (1) mengukur perbedaan kemampuan menulis teks bahasa Jerman mahasiswa sebelum dan sesudah menggunakan Meta AI dan (2) mengetahui sejauh mana Meta AI dapat membantu meningkatkan kemampuan menulis teks bahasa Jerman mahasiswa. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain quasi experiment tipe pretest-posttest control group design. Sampel penelitian terdiri atas mahasiswa mata kuliah Schriftliche Kommunikation Universitas Negeri Malang yang terbagi dalam kelas eksperimen dan kelas kontrol. Data diperoleh melalui tes esai, tugas menulis, dan angket, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif, uji t, dan effect size Cohen’s d. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan menulis mahasiswa pada kelas eksperimen meningkat sebesar 10,7 poin setelah menggunakan Meta AI. Hasil uji statistik menunjukkan terdapat perbedaan yang signifikan antara kemampuan menulis sebelum dan sesudah perlakuan dengan nilai t = 3,613, p = 0,003 < 0,05, dan effect size Cohen’s d = 0,968, yang menunjukkan kategori efek kuat. Hasil tugas dan angket menunjukkan bahwa Meta AI membantu mahasiswa mengembangkan ide, memperkaya kosakata, memahami penggunaan artikel (der, die, dan das), memperbaiki tata bahasa, serta menyusun teks yang lebih terstruktur. Dengan demikian, Meta AI dapat menjadi teknologi pendukung yang memberikan bantuan secara bertahap dalam proses pembelajaran menulis bahasa Jerman.

Physical Education, Health, and Sport (PJOK) learning outcomes in elementary schools frequently remain suboptimal due to conventional instructional methods that fail to engage multiple sensory modalities. This empirical gap is evident in students' low mastery of flexibility movement concepts, where varied learning preferences are rarely facilitated simultaneously. Consequently, adopting an integrated learning model that synthesizes bodily movement with cognitive engagement is critical. This study aims to determine the effect of the SAVI (Somatic, Auditory, Visualization, and Intellectually) learning model on fourth-grade students' PJOK learning outcomes at SD Negeri 068332 Simalingkar during the 2025/2026 academic year. A quantitative pre-experimental method with a one-group pretest-posttest design was conducted on 30 students selected via total sampling. Data were gathered through expert-validated achievement tests and student response questionnaires. Findings revealed that the initial pretest average of 50.66 significantly increased to 78.50 in the posttest assessment. The paired sample t-test generated a t_"value" greater than the critical t_"table" (9.859≥1.697) at a significance level of 0.000 (p<0.05). Thus, the SAVI learning model exerts a statistically significant positive effect on enhancing primary students' physical education outcomes. ABSTRAK Hasil belajar Pendidikan Jasmani, Olahraga, dan Kesehatan (PJOK) di sekolah dasar sering kali belum mencapai ketuntasan optimal karena dominasi pembelajaran konvensional yang kurang mengintegrasikan seluruh modalitas sensori siswa. Kesenjangan ini tampak pada rendahnya pemahaman konsep serta keterampilan gerak materi kelenturan yang belum mengakomodasi keberagaman gaya belajar anak secara simultan. Oleh karena itu, penerapan model pembelajaran terpadu yang memadukan aktivitas fisik dan proses berpikir menjadi sangat penting untuk diterapkan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji pengaruh model pembelajaran SAVI (Somatic, Auditory, Visualization, and Intellectually) terhadap peningkatan hasil belajar PJOK siswa kelas IV SD Negeri 068332 Simalingkar Tahun Pembelajaran 2025/2026. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain pre-experimental tipe one-group pretest-posttest design diterapkan terhadap 30 siswa yang dipilih melalui teknik total sampling. Pengumpulan data menggunakan instrumen tes hasil belajar kognitif dan psikomotorik yang telah divalidasi ahli serta angket respon siswa. Hasil penelitian membuktikan bahwa rata-rata pretest sebesar 50,66 meningkat secara signifikan menjadi 78,50 pada perolehan posttest. Hasil analisis uji hipotesis menunjukkan nilai t_"hitung" lebih besar daripada t_"tabel" (9,859≥1,697) dengan signifikansi 0,000 (p<0,05). Dengan demikian, model pembelajaran SAVI berpengaruh signifikan dalam meningkatkan hasil belajar PJOK materi kelenturan pada siswa sekolah dasar.

The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed organizational processes and increased the demand for talent with specialized knowledge and skills to integrate AI into business activities. This study aims to examine the role of artificial intelligence talent in building organizational competitive advantage. The research employs a systematic literature review (SLR) by identifying, evaluating, and synthesizing relevant national and international studies on AI talent, AI skills, human capital, innovation, organizational performance, and competitive advantage. The findings indicate that AI talent contributes to competitive advantage through innovation, productivity improvement, data-driven decision-making, knowledge utilization, and organizational AI capabilities. Furthermore, AI talent requires not only technical expertise but also analytical, collaborative, and business-oriented competencies. Theoretically, this study positions AI talent as a strategic human capital resource within the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities perspectives. Practically, the findings emphasize the importance of strategic recruitment, continuous upskilling and reskilling, and knowledge sharing to optimize AI talent. Overall, AI talent plays an important role in transforming technological capabilities into sustainable competitive advantage.

Introduction Organizations increasingly adopt Artificial Intelligence (AI) to gain competitive advantages, but anticipated benefits may not materialize when employee needs and work design aspects are neglected. Job crafting—employees' self-initiated work adjustments—may represent an important mechanism linking perceived AI support with work outcomes, but its role in the context of AI-supported work remains underexplored. Drawing on job demands-resources theory, this cross-sectional study examines relationships between perceived AI support, approach and avoidance crafting, and how these pathways may mediate associations with job satisfaction, perceived productivity, work engagement, turnover intentions, and burnout. Methods Data were collected via an online survey of employees engaged in information and knowledge work in Germany, who use AI systems ( n = 695). Using structural equation modeling, a mediation model with approach and avoidance crafting as parallel mediators was tested. Results Results revealed that perceived AI support was positively associated with both approach and avoidance crafting. Approach crafting emerged as a dominant pathway, being positively associated with job satisfaction, work engagement, and perceived productivity and negatively associated with burnout and turnover intentions. Avoidance crafting showed contrary associations. Total effects of AI support through approach and avoidance crafting indicated associations with increased job satisfaction, perceived productivity and work engagement, and reduced burnout. Discussion These findings extend job crafting theory to AI-supported work by indicating that perceived AI support functions as a job resource that is associated with distinct crafting pathways. Organizations should implement AI systems that employees perceive as supportive, thereby providing a resource that enables job crafting, and further promote approach over avoidance crafting through corresponding work design measures and targeted personnel development.

BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI)- supported ergonomic assessments identify occupational musculoskeletal risks, though agreement with physiotherapist-based evaluations remains insufficiently studied to date.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the relationship between AI-assisted ergonomic risk analysis and physiotherapist-based ergonomic assessments among young adults performing desk-based work.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 133 desk workers aged 18-25 years who used electronic devices at their desks for more than 4 h per day. Ergonomic risk was evaluated using two methods: Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) and OpenAI ChatGPT. Pain intensity was measured with the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Pearson correlation analysis assessed the relationship between RULA and ChatGPT scores. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess discriminative performance and determine the optimal cutoff value for the AI-based assessment.ResultsThe participants' (48.9% females and 51.1% males) mean age was 24.02 ± 6.34 years. The mean RULA and ChatGPT scores were 4.65 ± 1.31 and 45.71 ± 16.31. A statistically significant positive correlation was observed between ChatGPT and RULA scores (r = 0.304, p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed moderate discriminatory performance for the AI-based assessment (AUC = 0.659; 95% CI: 0.565-0.752; p = 0.002). The optimal cutoff for the ergonomic risk analysis using ChatGPT was 42.5, yielding 72.4% sensitivity and 56.0% specificity.ConclusionsAI-assisted ergonomic risk analysis showed moderate agreement with conventional physiotherapist-based assessments and may serve as a rapid, accessible screening tool for desk workers. Nevertheless, clinical interpretation by healthcare professionals remains essential for accurate ergonomic evaluation and decision-making.
